newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:
* Tony Blair and the Labour Party stormed to power in Britain's national election, putting an end to 18 years of Conservative rule in the country.
* Man in the News: Tony Blair, Britain's new 43-year-old Prime Minister, has engineered a remarkable make-over of the country's Labour Party, defining it as pro-business.
* White House and Congressional negotiators agreed on most elements of an historic budget accord although they failed to reach a final pact due to tax cut-related differences.
* The nonprofit group that has run the Brookhaven National Laboratory since it began 50 years ago was dismissed by the Federal Government, which raised safety issues.
* Democratic Congressional leaders accused the Clinton Administration of working on a budget deal with Republicans behind their back.
* According to intelligence reports, France attempted to prop up Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko in January through a covert military operation against the rebel forces.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Administration was seen taking a cautious approach to regulating tobacco, focusing for the meantime on the politics of tobacco regulation.
* Politicians in Albany, New York's capitol, are targetting wealthy tenants who are seen as abusing the rent control system.
